title: Seat a baby bottle in a twin warmer's free well beside a warming one, then start it
instruction: Put the bottle from the tray into the warmer's free well and start that well. Leave the bottle already warming undisturbed.
context: Warming a baby's bottle is an everyday job for parents and carers. A two-well warmer warms two children's bottles at once, so the second bottle often goes in beside one that is already warming. Carers often do this one-handed with a baby on the other arm; the task is one-armed and does not claim to need two. The hard parts, in order: (1) the grip: the free well is only 5 mm wider each side than the 62 mm bottle and the open pads cannot enter it, so the 0.20 kg bottle is pinched high on its body and must stay upright in the carry; (2) the lowering: straight down 50 mm with no lead-in chamfer, 48 mm from the warming bottle, which a 3 mm nudge, a 2 mm lift or a 3 degree tilt counts as disturbed; (3) the order: seat first, then push that well's sprung button 3 mm of its 5 mm; a push before seating is a dry start, a second push turns it off; (4) let go and withdraw without dragging the bottle.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; millimetres; x forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up from the table top; arm bases at y +305 and -305. The table plays the nursery counter. (1) Bottle warmer, a fixed unheated fixture (taped down in a trial), cream, 110 (x) by 320 (y) by 60 tall, centre (x 260, y 0), front face at x 205. Build: a 10 mm plywood base sheet under a 50 mm block (two 25 mm sheets glued), both 110 by 320. Two bores through the block, 72 across (hole saw), axes at y +55 and y -55 (x 260): each well is 50 deep, floor 10 above the counter; walls 19 or more thick all round, 38 between the wells (the sim's bores are 16-sided, 72 across the flats). Each well has its own green push button on the top at x 230, y +143 (well +55) and y -143 (well -55), made as: a 19 mm bore 30 deep from the top; an 18 mm hardwood dowel plunger 24 long, 6 mm proud at rest, with an 8 mm long slot cut in its side; a 3 mm steel pin through the block's side wall into the slot, which stops the plunger at rest and at 5 mm of travel; under it a steel compression spring (outer diameter 15 to 17 mm, free length 12 mm, solid height 7 mm or less, rate about 0.25 N/mm, 1.25 N at the stop), picked by force gauge. No wiring: a button counts as pushed when it is in 3 mm or more. Acceptance checks with calipers and a force gauge: bore 72 plus or minus 1 mm, depth 50 plus or minus 1, centres 110 plus or minus 1; plunger proud 6 plus or minus 0.5, travel 5 plus or minus 0.5, force at the stop 0.75 to 2 N; it springs fully back. One push turns its well on, the next off (tracked by the scorer or an observer). (2) Splashback, fixed: a tiled wall 20 thick, 200 tall, x 320 to 340, y -200 to +200, 5 mm behind the warmer. (3) Bottle tray, fixed: grey plastic, 100 by 100 by 12, wall 4, floor 4, centre (x 270, y -250). (4) Neighbour's bottle, loose: 260 mL polypropylene feeding bottle, 62 across, 135 tall with its screw collar (pink, 110 to 120 up) and cap hood (white, 52 across), 0.20 kg with a 150 mL feed (water in a trial), standing upright on the floor of the +55 well, its axis on the well's. (5) The loose bottle, identical but with a blue collar, standing on the tray's floor at (x 270, y -250). The empty -55 well is the free one. Nothing else is on the counter. Both arms start at the ready pose, grippers open.
scoring: Read from the poses of both bottles, the two buttons and both grippers; the warmer is fixed, its wells and outline are design values. Latched over the whole trial: score 0 if either bottle's lowest point goes more than 50 mm below the counter top (falls off), either bottle's axis tilts over 30 degrees (spill), or the neighbour's centre is more than 12 mm off its well's axis or its base more than 30 mm up (knocked out). Disturbed (latched, caps the score): the neighbour's centre is ever 3 mm or more from where it stood, its base ever 2 mm up, its axis ever over 3 degrees off vertical, or its own button ever pushed 1 mm; moved and put back still counts. Push: the free well's button in 3 mm or more; it counts again only after the button is back out to 1 mm. Dry start (latched, caps the score like disturbed): a push while the loose bottle is not seated. End state at the last step. Started: an odd number of pushes (the well is on). Seated: the loose bottle's centre within 6 mm of the free well's axis, its base within 2 mm of the well floor's top, its axis within 3 degrees of vertical. Resting: not seated, its base on the warmer's top (lowest point within 3 mm of it, centre over the outline) or leaning in the free well (centre within 36 mm of its axis, lowest point between 2 mm under the floor's top and the warmer's top). Hands off: on every step of the last 1 s both grippers' finger zones are 30 mm or more from both bottles and the warmer, and over that 1 s each bottle moves under 5 mm and turns under 5 degrees (visible motion); a button is not read for stillness, its state is the pushes counted above. Score: 1.0 seated, started, hands off; 0.75 seated, started, not yet hands off; 0.5 seated, not started; 0.25 resting, hands off; 0 otherwise or any 0 latch. If disturbed or dry started, the score is at most 0.5 when started and at most 0.25 when not. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0. Success: 1.0 held for 1 s. In a real trial, per condition: fall, a rule from the counter to the bottle's base; spill, a 30 degree angle gauge; knocked out, by eye against the well; seated centre, a rule from the well wall to the bottle on opposite sides along two perpendicular lines (half the difference of each opposite pair is the centre offset: at most 6 mm); base, a rule from the warmer's top face to a line drawn round the bottle at its fully seated height (within 2 mm); axis, a 3 degree angle gauge; disturbed, a pencil ring round the neighbour's base, a rule (3 mm), a 3 degree angle gauge, a top-down 30 fps video against a grid card, and a side-view 30 fps video with a tape mark on the neighbour 2 mm above the well rim for any lift in between; button, a rule on its travel (3 mm, 1 mm) and the video for the order; hands off, a 30 mm spacer against each hand and the 30 fps video of the last 1 s: no bottle visibly moves or turns against a taped mark on the counter (5 mm, 5 degrees).
fidelity: Rigid bodies. The warmer is an unheated, unwired fixed stand-in, not a sold model: wells 16-sided, 72 mm across the flats (real build: round bores); a button on its top per well, a sprung slider, 250 N/m, 5 mm travel (est). The bottle is a 62 by 135 mm stand-in without a nipple, 0.20 kg fixed mass, smaller than sold 260 mL bottles (Philips Avent SCY903/01: 71 by 166 mm). Nothing heats or lights. Default friction.
reset_notes: Stand the neighbour's bottle on the floor of the +y well, centred; stand the other on the tray at (x 270, y -250). Both buttons out (check proud 6 mm). Bottles hold 150 mL of water at room temperature; wipe up spills. Nothing is consumed or heated.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0; demo: 1.0 (588 steps); one arm idle: 1.0 (left idle), 0.0 (right idle)
